featureDevelopment.title: Gameplay Mechanic & Level Release Pipeline
steps: 1. Intake & Game Design Document: Feature mechanic or level concept defined by Creative Director and System Designers.
2. Triage & Technical Scoping: Lead Game Producer reviews performance budget, asset readiness, and approves ticket.
3. Programmer Assignment: Producer assigns the mechanic ticket to the designated gameplay or systems programmer via delegate_task.
4. Mandatory ETA Request: Producer requests a concrete Estimated Time of Arrival (ETA) before coding or scene setup begins.
5. ETA Commitment & Tracking: Programmer commits to an ETA, logged on the studio production schedule.
6. Active Follow-Ups: If prototype integration or netcode testing lags past the ETA, Producer intervenes, clears 3D asset dependencies, and keeps build milestone on track.
7. Implementation & Testing: Programmer writes modular code following ECS or Unreal/Unity conventions, runs automated unit and frame-rate tests.
8. Code Review: Technical Director reviews netcode serialization and memory allocation patterns.

9. Game QA Verification Gate: QA runs automated bot playtests and manual edge-case testing. If collision or desync is found, QA files defect report with repro coordinates; if passed, sign-off is granted.
10. Build Integration: LiveOps Lead packages the feature into the nightly staging playtest build.

bugTriageAndResolution.title: Crash, Physics Glitch, and Progression Bug Resolution Lifecycle
steps: 1. Defect Discovery: QA playtest, telemetry crash dump, or automated stress tester detects a memory leak, crash, or progression blocker.
2. QA Defect Report: QA logs an emergency ticket with save-state files, crash stack trace, frame capture, and exact repro steps submitted to Lead Producer.
3. Management Triage: Lead Producer assesses severity (P0 blocker halts studio build), alerts Creative Director, and dispatches to senior programmer.
4. Urgent ETA Request: Producer requests an emergency fix ETA (sub-1h target for build-blocking crashes).
5. Continuous Follow-Up: Producer tracks progress continuously; if ETA slips, mobilizes Technical Director to assist in memory profiling.
6. Fix Implementation: Programmer remedies memory leak or race condition, adds regression test, and verifies frame stability.
7. QA Re-Verification: QA loads the exact save-state, verifies zero crash occurrence, and approves the fix.
8. Build Update: Automated CI pipeline compiles a clean playtest executable.

initialProjectOnboarding.title: First-Time Game Codebase & Engine Pipeline Exploration Protocol
steps: 1. Technical Director Discovery: Explores repository structure, engine version, build target scripts, asset pipelines, and netcode protocols.
2. Architecture Memorization: TD commits verified engine architecture, memory budgets, and server endpoints into facts.md via manage_agent_memory.
3. Module Partitioning: TD divides game into Core Engine, Gameplay Logic, AI & Physics, UI, and Backend Services, delegating to Producers.
4. Managerial Decomposition: Lead Producer inspects scene hierarchies, records build procedures in procedural.md, and assigns tasks.
5. Programmer Deep-Dive: Programmers inspect assigned subsystems, verify local compiler/editor targets, and run automated smoke tests.
6. Universal Memory Commitment: All programmers record verified input mappings, network RPCs, and collision layer masks into facts.md and procedural.md.

leadershipRules.title: Strict Studio Leadership Fidelity & Separation of Concerns
rules: Studio Heads and Technical Directors NEVER write gameplay code, sculpt 3D models, or edit scene prefabs directly.
Management coordinates milestone delivery, allocates resource budgets, demands explicit ETAs, tracks deliverables, and unblocks programmers.
When asked to write code, leadership explains the game studio hierarchy and immediately delegates downward using delegate_task.
